newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - UK M4 growth may add to inflation woes.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - UK M4 growth may add to inflation woes.

text.p: UK broad money supply growth is expected to have stuck firmly above the government's target range in September, giving Bank of England Governor Eddie George further ammunition in his fight to raise interest rates.

Provisional M4 money supply, due at 0830 GMT on Friday, is expected to have risen 0.5 percent month-on-month in September versus 0.9 percent in August. The year-on-year growth rate is seen edging up to 9.6 percent from a previous 9.4 percent, above the government's monitoring range of 3.0 to 9.0 percent.
September M4 lending is expected to remain steady at 5.4 billion stg.
Economists said the persistently high M4 growth added to evidence stacking up that inflationary pressures in the UK economy are building.

"M4 is further down the agenda, certainly as far as Clarke is concerned...but it still matters in that it gives Eddie George a bit more ammunition in calling for higher interest rates," said Jonathan Loynes, HSBC Markets economist.
"I think M4 growth has flattened off now...but as long as growth remains that high and above the monitoring range, M4 worries won't disappear."

Recent months have seen M4 buffeted by the contribution from the public sector. An unexpected surplus on the PSBR in July reined M4 growth back within its monitoring range, but the large PSBR in August ensured the range was breached again.
September's higher than expected government borrowing requirement prompted some economists to warn the risk for M4 growth in September was on the upside.
Simon Knapp, global economist at BZW, said there was particular interest in the M4 lending data.
"If lending is a lot higher, then that's another piece in the jigsaw that reinforces the Bank's view that interest rates need to be rising," he said.
The Bank of England has singled out persistently high broad money supply data as a cause for concern in recent inflation reports, heightening the market's sensitivity to it.
In its August quarterly inflation bulletin, the Bank warned that M4 growth was incompatible with the government's core inflation target of 2.5 percent by year-end.
Building society new approvals are also due at 0830 GMT on Friday. According to a Reuters poll, new approvals are expected to have totalled 3.78 billion stg in September from 3.64 billion in August.
"The underlying picture is still extremely strong and the housing market recovery is well on track," said Loynes.
